classes.name: Izbori za zastupnike u Hrvatski sabor
classes.name_en: Croatian Parliament elections
classes.finest_note: Results by polling station (biračko mjesto) in the commission's zip files from 2000; 1992 and 1995 only as scanned reports by electoral district and municipality.
classes.note: Zastupnički dom of the bicameral Sabor 1992–2001, then the unicameral Hrvatski sabor. Since 2000: ten 14-seat list-PR districts (5% threshold per district, D'Hondt), district XI for voters abroad, and district XII for the 8 national-minority seats (3 Serb seats by block vote, others single seats). 1992 and 1995 were mixed systems with single-member districts and a national list.

cadence.vacancy_rule: Ustav art. 73 and 77: the Sabor may dissolve itself by majority vote, or the President dissolves it on the Government's proposal; elections within 60 days of dissolution or the end of term.

access.evidence: Per-polling-station results for every Sabor election from 2000.
Scanned reports by electoral district and national list; 1995 as one scanned report.

classes.name: Izbori za zastupnike u Županijski dom Sabora
classes.name_en: Chamber of Counties elections
classes.note: Upper chamber of 3 members per county and the City of Zagreb by list PR, plus up to 5 members appointed by the President. Abolished by the constitutional amendment of 28 March 2001 (NN 28/2001).

access.evidence: One scanned report per election with list votes and seats by county.

classes.name: Izbori za predsjednika Republike Hrvatske
classes.name_en: Presidential elections
classes.finest_note: Per-polling-station results from 2000; 1992 and 1997 as scanned reports by municipality.

cadence.runoff_rule: A candidate needs a majority of those who voted; otherwise the top two meet 14 days later (Ustav art. 94).
cadence.vacancy_rule: Ustav art. 97: election within 60 days of a vacancy.

access.evidence: Per-polling-station results for both rounds from 2000.
Scanned reports by municipality and abroad.

classes.name: Državni referendum
classes.name_en: National referendums
classes.note: Called by the Sabor, by the President on the Government's proposal, or on a citizens' initiative of 10% of voters (Ustav art. 87). Held in 1991 (independence, under the Socialist Republic's constitution), 2012 (EU accession), and 2013 (definition of marriage). Initiatives that failed the signature count never reached a ballot.

access.evidence: Per-polling-station results for 2012 and 2013; 1991 as a scanned report.

dates.note: Two questions: Croatia as a sovereign state that may join a union of sovereign states, and Croatia remaining in Yugoslavia as a federal state.

dates.quote: Referendum o pristupanju Hrvatske Europskoj uniji (22.01.2012.)

classes.name: Izbori za članove u Europski parlament iz Republike Hrvatske
classes.name_en: European Parliament elections in Croatia
classes.note: One national constituency, open lists with a preference vote, D'Hondt with a 5% threshold. 12 seats in 2013 and 2024, 11 in 2014 and 2019 (12 from 1 February 2020).

access.evidence: Per-polling-station results for 2013, 2014, 2019, and 2024, the same layout as the Sabor files.

classes.name: Izbori za zastupnike u Sabor Socijalističke Republike Hrvatske 1990.
classes.name_en: 1990 multiparty election to the three chambers of the Sabor
classes.note: First multiparty election: Društveno-političko vijeće (80 single-member districts), Vijeće općina (one seat per municipality), and Vijeće udruženog rada (160 seats elected by workplace electorates), two-round majority system. First round 22–23 April, second round 6–7 May 1990.

access.evidence: Six scanned reports (76 to 152 pages each) with candidate votes, registered voters, and turnout per district and round for each chamber.

dates.quote: IZBORI ZA ZASTUPNIKE U HRVATSKI SABOR (22.04.1990.): Društveno političko vijeće; Vijeće općina; Vijeće udruženog rada

classes.name: Izbori za Sabor NR/SR Hrvatske 1946.–1986.
classes.name_en: Sabor elections of the People's and Socialist Republic, 1946–1986
classes.note: Single-list elections to the Constituent Sabor (1946) and the Sabor (1950, 1953, 1958, 1963, 1967, 1969); from 1974 the chambers were filled by delegations chosen in a multi-stage delegate system (1974, 1978, 1982, 1986), so only the first stage had a popular vote.

dates.note: Eleven elections; dates and returns are in the Narodne novine of each year and the statistical office's election bulletins, not yet listed here.

classes.name: Izbori za Hrvatski sabor (Kraljevine Hrvatska i Slavonija, Dalmatinski i Istarski sabor)
classes.name_en: Elections to the Croatian-Slavonian Sabor and the Dalmatian and Istrian Diets, 1848–1913
classes.note: The Croatian-Slavonian Sabor was first elected in 1848 and then in 1861, 1865, 1867, 1871, 1872, 1875, 1878, 1881, 1884, 1887, 1892, 1897, 1901, 1906, 1908, 1910, 1911, and 1913 under a census franchise, by single-member electoral districts with public voting; the Dalmatian Diet (1861–1908) and the Istrian Diet (1861–1914) were Austrian crown-land diets elected by curiae. Returns survive in the Sabor's stenographic records and the official Narodne novine of each year.

dates.note: About 19 Croatian-Slavonian Sabor elections plus the Dalmatian and Istrian Diets; not yet listed.

classes.name: Izbori za članove županijskih skupština i Gradske skupštine Grada Zagreba
classes.name_en: County assembly and Zagreb City Assembly elections
classes.finest_note: Polling-station results in the zip files from 2013; 1993–2009 as scanned or typeset reports by county.
classes.note: List PR in one county-wide constituency, 5% threshold, D'Hondt, with extra seats to keep minority representation (Zakon o lokalnim izborima art. 20). The City of Zagreb is a town with county status, so its Gradska skupština is counted here. Zagreb also elected its assembly early on 29 October 1995.

cadence.vacancy_rule: Early elections after dissolution (Zakon o lokalnim izborima art. 105).

access.evidence: Per-polling-station results for every county assembly from 2013.
One report per county: list votes and seats for 1993, 1997, and 2001; elected members only for 2005 and 2009.

dates.note: The commission's archive page heads this election 25.05.2001; polling day was Sunday 20 May 2001.
Early (prijevremeni) and supplementary (dopunski) local elections: the commission's archive lists 76 such days from 11 July 2010 to 31 May 2026; contests not yet counted.

classes.name: Izbori za župane i gradonačelnika Grada Zagreba
classes.name_en: County prefect and Zagreb mayoral elections
classes.note: Directly elected since 2009 with their deputies on the same ticket; before 2009 the assembly chose the župan (see posredni).

cadence.runoff_rule: More than half of the votes cast elects; otherwise the top two meet on the 14th day (Zakon o lokalnim izborima art. 94).

access.evidence: Per-polling-station results for both rounds from 2013; 2009 elected candidates only.

classes.name: Izbori za članove gradskih i općinskih vijeća
classes.name_en: Town and municipal council elections
classes.finest_note: Polling-station results in the zip files from 2013.
classes.note: List PR in one constituency per town or municipality, 5% threshold, D'Hondt; seats for national minorities added where the Constitutional Act requires them. 1993–1997 used a mixed system.

cadence.vacancy_rule: Early elections after dissolution (Zakon o lokalnim izborima art. 105).

access.evidence: Per-polling-station results for every town and municipal council from 2013.
One report per county: list votes and seats per town and municipality for 1993, 1997, and 2001; elected members only for 2005 and 2009.

access.platform: Arhiva izbora (DIP): prijevremeni i dopunski izbori
access.evidence: 76 early and supplementary election days from 2010 to 2026.

dates.note: The commission's archive page heads this election 25.05.2001; polling day was Sunday 20 May 2001.
Early (prijevremeni) and supplementary (dopunski) local elections: the commission's archive lists 76 such days from 11 July 2010 to 31 May 2026; contests not yet counted.

classes.name: Izbori za gradonačelnike i općinske načelnike
classes.name_en: Mayoral elections
classes.note: Directly elected since 2009 with their deputies on the same ticket; before 2009 the council chose the mayor (see posredni). Recall by local referendum is possible.

cadence.runoff_rule: More than half of the votes cast elects; otherwise the top two meet on the 14th day (Zakon o lokalnim izborima art. 94).

access.evidence: Per-polling-station results for both rounds from 2013; 2009 elected candidates only.

classes.name: Izbori za zamjenike župana, gradonačelnika i općinskih načelnika iz reda pripadnika nacionalnih manjina
classes.name_en: Elections of deputy prefects and deputy mayors from national minorities
classes.note: Where a minority makes up enough of the population, its members elect a deputy župan or deputy mayor in a separate contest held with the local elections (Ustavni zakon o pravima nacionalnih manjina art. 20; Zakon o lokalnim izborima art. 96–97); also held as supplementary elections when a contest fails.

access.evidence: Deputy contests sit beside the mayoral contests in the local election files from 2013.

classes.name: Lokalni i savjetodavni referendumi
classes.name_en: Local, recall, and consultative referendums
classes.note: Local referendums called by a council, the mayor, or 20% of voters, including recall votes on a mayor or župan since 2009; and consultative referendums on boundary changes, which the state commission ran for 1996 (Zakon o referendumu arts. 23–26). No central list of local referendums.

access.evidence: Scanned report on the 2 June 1996 consultative referendums, one decision per area.

dates.quote: utvrđuje i objavljuje službene rezultate provedenog glasovanja na savjetodavnom referendumu održanom dana 2. lipnja 1996. godine

classes.name: Izbori za skupštine općina (narodni odbori 1946.–1963., skupštine općina 1963.–1990.)
classes.name_en: Socialist-era municipal assembly elections, through the 1990 multiparty vote
classes.note: People's committees from 1946, then municipal assemblies; delegate system from 1974. The last, held with the Sabor on 22 April and 6 May 1990, elected the three-chamber assemblies of 102 municipalities in multiparty contests; no central report is in the commission's archive.

dates.note: Communal elections not yet listed; the last was the 1990 multiparty round.

classes.name: Izbori za članove vijeća i predstavnike nacionalnih manjina
classes.name_en: National minority council and representative elections
classes.note: Members of each recognized national minority elect a council (10, 15, or 25 members) or a single representative in each county, town, and municipality where the minority reaches the legal thresholds (Ustavni zakon o pravima nacionalnih manjina arts. 23–24). Plurality: the candidates with the most votes win.

access.evidence: Elected candidates by county (2003–2015) and by unit (2019, 2023); vote counts per candidate in the per-unit reports from 2019.

classes.name: Izbori za vijeća mjesnih odbora i gradskih četvrti
classes.name_en: Local committee and city district council elections
classes.note: Councils of local committees (mjesni odbori) and of city districts (gradske četvrti, mainly Zagreb's 17).
classes.disposition_reason: Each town or municipality calls and runs these under its own statute and decision (Zakon o lokalnoj i područnoj (regionalnoj) samoupravi arts. 57–61); the State Electoral Commission neither runs nor compiles them, and no register lists the units or their returns.

classes.name: Posredni izbori
classes.name_en: Indirect elections
classes.disposition_reason: Officers chosen by elected bodies: the Prime Minister and Government (Sabor vote of confidence), the Speaker, Constitutional Court judges, and the Ombudsman by the Sabor; the President of the Presidency by the Sabor in 1990; župans and mayors by their assemblies and councils before 2009; council and assembly chairs. No electorate votes.

classes.name: Izbor sudaca porotnika i sudaca
classes.name_en: Lay judges and judges
classes.disposition_reason: No judge is elected by voters: judges are appointed by the State Judicial Council (Ustav art. 124), and lay judges are named by county assemblies; no electorate votes.

classes.name: Izbori u komorama, sveučilištima, radničkim vijećima i strankama
classes.name_en: Chamber, university, works council, and party elections
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the bodies themselves for their members (professional and economic chambers, universities, works councils, and party primaries); the law provides no state-run nominating contest, and no electoral authority certifies these for a territorial electorate.
